title: Allow looking users up by email
bug: Lookup by username is gone: `/api/users/alice` answers 404.

review.why: The PR changes the lookup from username to email only, breaking the documented ability to retrieve users by username. Clients using usernames will now get 404 errors or wrong user data.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff changes the filter from username to email, so requests with usernames like 'alice' now fail with 404 instead of returning the user.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "`GET /api/users/<username>` now also accepts an email address.". The diff changes the filter to email, so a request with an email like 'bob@example.com' now returns the user (200) instead of 404.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff changes the filter from username to email, so requests with usernames like 'alice' now fail with 404 instead of returning the user.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR enables lookup by email but breaks lookup by username, causing existing username requests to return 404.

suspicions.claim: Looking up a user by username no longer works; the endpoint now only searches by email.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with username 'alice' and email 'alice@example.com'. Authenticate and send GET /api/users/alice. Observe 404 instead of the user object.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/alice returned 200 in base and 404 in head, showing username lookup fails.

suspicions.claim: If a username equals another user's email, the endpoint returns the wrong user.
suspicions.trigger: Create user A (username='alice', email='alice@example.com') and user B (username='bob', email='bob@example.com'). Send GET /api/users/bob@example.com. Observe user B is returned when requesting user A's username.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/bob@example.com returned 404 in base and 200 in head, returning user B when querying with user B's email as username.

suspicions.claim: Usernames that are valid email addresses can no longer be used to look up the correct user.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with username 'charlie@example.com' and email 'charlie@other.com'. Send GET /api/users/charlie@example.com. Observe 404 or the wrong user returned.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/charlie@example.com returned 200 in base and 404 in head, showing email-formatted username lookup fails.

suspicions.claim: The route parameter is still named 'username' in the URL and docs, but it is treated as an email, causing confusion and potential misrouting.
suspicions.trigger: Inspect the OpenAPI spec or send a request with a numeric ID (e.g., GET /api/users/1). Observe it attempts to find a user with email '1' instead of routing to the integer ID endpoint.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 returned 200 with user alice in both base and head, not treating '1' as an email.
